claims.text: Adding 1–3 wt% Ti to a MnNiSi-based magnetocaloric alloy will improve its mechanical performance.
Ti addition will induce grain refinement in the MnNiSi-based alloy.
Ti addition followed by homogenization will produce uniformly distributed Ti-rich precipitates.
Grain refinement can enhance tensile strength while retaining useful ductility.
Fine Ti-rich precipitates will hinder dislocation motion in the MnNiSi-based alloy.
Fine Ti-rich precipitates will hinder crack propagation and thereby enhance toughness.
The Ti-induced refined microstructure and precipitates will increase tensile strength and fracture toughness relative to an identically processed Ti-free baseline.
The Ti addition will not significantly perturb the magnetic exchange interactions responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
Minor alloying can shift a magnetocaloric transition temperature while causing relatively small changes in peak magnetic entropy change.
The Ti-doped MnNiSi-based alloy will retain a large magnetocaloric effect.
Peak magnetic entropy change in the Ti-doped alloy will differ by less than 10% from the Ti-free baseline.
The initial MnNiSi-based alloy has a robust magnetocaloric effect near its transition temperature but limited mechanical toughness.
The relevant magnetic transition is expected around room temperature to slightly above room temperature.
The predicted improvement is conditional on arc melting followed by homogenization and operation near the magnetic transition.
Substantially changing the processing route or operating temperature may change the predicted response.
The magnitudes of mechanical enhancement and magnetocaloric retention may depend on Ti content and heat-treatment parameters.
